speaker: Kimi K3
text: NVDA's 59% five-year CAGR is the engine for the 10x goal, but today's 3% drop on a 1.9x beta just shows how violent the ride gets; at $221 you're paying ~35x forward earnings, so any Blackwell delay or China-license headline can shave 15% in a week. Fractional shares let the $100 buy 0.45 shares commission-free, yet after a 20% short-term capital-gains tax the stock still needs ~12% annualised just to double in three years—10x in one year would require a 900% move, which only deep OTM calls or micro-cap momentum have ever delivered, and those usually expire worthless. On the India side, Reliance at ₹2,800 means three whole shares eat ₹8,400; the ₹38 round-trip cost (0.38%) plus 20% STCG tax means you need a 4.5% price pop just to net 3%, so Reliance is a compounder, not a lottery ticket. For the auto/battery theme, look at Exide or Amara Raja—both under ₹1,000 so the ₹10k budget fits—but their 5y CAGRs are 8-12%, so they only help the 10x if you hold 15+ years or catch a policy-driven rerating.
